summary: The narrator recounts a grudge against Sibley, a girl from fifth grade who mocked them, and a classmate named Dakota, after a school PowerPoint on Minnesota history about Henry Hastings Sibley. The narrator describes Sibley's treatment of the Dakota, including a deceptive treaty and the condemnation of 300 Indians after the Dakota war, with 38 hanged after Lincoln intervened. After being sent to the school psychologist over the incident, the narrator plans revenge on three girls by creating a fake boy persona online to turn them against each other, and studies each girl to find a weakness to exploit.
one_line: A student's account of a school PowerPoint on Henry Hastings Sibley and the revenge plot that followed against three girls who bullied her.
key_facts: The narrator's fifth-grade PowerPoint was about Henry Hastings Sibley, the first governor of Minnesota.
Sibley got the Dakota to sign a document they thought was a copy of a treaty, but it was a trick to take away their money.
The teacher had accused the narrator of making up the treaty trick until the narrator showed a book with footnotes.
After the Dakota war, Sibley was in charge of a trial that got 300 Indians condemned to death.
The narrator says only 38 were hanged because Lincoln said it was too many.
Sibley, the girl, and a classmate named Dakota were upset and said the narrator was picking on them and using the race card.
The narrator said "This is about race, you idiots," and was sent to the school psychologist.
The narrator created fake Snapchat and Kik accounts for a cute, cool boy to privately chat with each of the three girls.
One girl, Lyndsay, sent embarrassing naked selfies to the fake account.
The narrator chose Rebecca's hair as her weakness, since she constantly played with it and freaked out over split ends.
Harper was described as the tough, meanest one of the three girls and was harder to crack.
The narrator spent a couple of weeks watching the three girls before devising the strategy.
